facts.text: In US construction, OSHA 29 CFR 1926.601(b)(4) and 1926.602(a)(9)(ii) require a reverse signal alarm audible above surrounding noise, or an observer, when the rear view is obstructed.
facts.quote: require a reverse signal alarm audible above surrounding noise, or an observer, when the rear view is obstructed.

facts.text: OSHA letters of interpretation accept a camera as removing the obstructed-rear-view trigger for the construction reverse-warning requirement if the camera truly provides the required clear view.
facts.quote: a camera can remove the "obstructed view" trigger if it truly provides the required clear view

facts.text: OSHA letters of interpretation accept radar or doppler warning as satisfying the construction reverse-warning requirement where the warning is adequate and timely.
facts.quote: radar or doppler warning can satisfy the requirement where it gives adequate warning in time.

facts.text: OSHA 29 CFR 1926.601(b)(4) and 1926.602(a)(9)(ii), applicable to construction, do not mandate automatic braking.
facts.quote: No automatic-brake mandate.

facts.text: MSHA 30 CFR 77.410 requires front-end loaders, forklifts, tractors, graders, trucks and similar mobile equipment in surface coal operations to have either a reverse alarm or discriminating detection using infrared, ultrasonic, radar, or another effective device.
facts.quote: requires, for front-end loaders, forklifts, tractors, graders, trucks and similar mobile equipment, either a reverse alarm or discriminating detection "using infrared, ultrasonic, radar, or another effective device"

facts.text: Under MSHA 30 CFR 77.410 for surface coal mobile equipment, the detection sensing area must give endangered persons adequate time to escape.
facts.quote: the sensing area must give endangered persons adequate time to escape

facts.text: MSHA 30 CFR 77.410 prescribes internal audible and visual warnings plus external audible warnings for surface coal mobile equipment.
facts.quote: internal audible and visual plus external audible warnings are prescribed.

facts.text: Lidar is not named in MSHA 30 CFR 77.410 and should not be described as approved under that regulation, although lidar could fall under “another effective device”.
facts.quote: Lidar is not named, so it should not be described as "approved", although it could fall under "another effective device".

facts.text: MSHA 30 CFR 77.410 for surface coal mobile equipment has no automatic braking requirement.
facts.quote: No automatic braking requirement.

facts.text: MSHA 30 CFR 56.14132 and 57.14132 require a reverse-activated alarm, specified alternatives, or an observer for self-propelled mobile equipment with an obstructed rear view in metal and non-metal mines.
facts.quote: require a reverse-activated alarm, specified alternatives, or an observer for self-propelled mobile equipment with an obstructed rear view

facts.text: Reverse alarms under MSHA 30 CFR 56.14132 and 57.14132 for metal and non-metal mines must be audible above surrounding noise.
facts.quote: alarms must be audible above surrounding noise.

facts.text: The final rule for MSHA 30 CFR 75.1732, concerning proximity detection systems on continuous mining machines in underground coal mines, was issued as 80 FR 2188 on 15 January 2015.
facts.quote: **MSHA 30 CFR 75.1732**, proximity detection systems on continuous mining machines in underground coal mines (final rule 80 FR 2188, 15 January 2015).

facts.text: MSHA 30 CFR 75.1732 is performance-based: proximity detection systems on continuous mining machines in underground coal mines must stop the machine before contacting a miner and must first give audible and visual warnings.
facts.quote: The rule is performance-based: the system must cause the machine to stop before contacting a miner and must give audible and visual warnings first.

facts.text: The 3 ft stopping distance and 5 ft warning distance proposed in 2011 were not adopted in MSHA 30 CFR 75.1732 for continuous mining machines in underground coal mines.
facts.quote: The 3 ft stop and 5 ft warning distances in the 2011 proposal were not adopted.
